sections.body: Home » Destinations » Lima » Archaeological Sites » Caral Caral Archaeological Site The Caral Archaeological Site is considered one of the oldest sites in America and has been recognized as a World Heritage Site by UNESCO. Caral is known for being the oldest city in America, with an age of approximately 5,000 years. It was discovered in 1994 by the Peruvian archaeologist Ruth Shady, who has led research and excavations at the site since then. The archaeological zone of Caral covers an area of approximately 66 hectares and is composed of a series of pyram ids, squares, and ceremonial buildings. The architecture of Caral is impressive, with monumental structures built with stone and mud. The stepped pyramids, which are the most recognizable symbol of Caral, stand out. In addition to its historical and archaeological significance, Caral is also a place of great natural beauty. It is surrounded by mountains and offers breathtaking views of the Supe Valley. The archaeological site has been prepared to welcome visitors, with trails and viewpoints that allow exploring and enjoying the majesty of Caral. History of the Caral Archaeological Site The Caralians built monumental architectural structures that still impress today with their size and design. Among them, the stepped pyramids stand out, considered the oldest in America. These pyramids, built with stone and mud, reach heights of up to 20 meters and have large squares at their tops. Temples and ceremonial squares have also been discovered, indicating the importance of religion and rituals in the life of this civilization. There is evidence that Caral was a significant political and religious center in its time, with a complex social organization. Caral’s urban planning is also admirable. The city is divided into different sectors, each with its own function. For example, residential areas, administrative areas, and areas for agricultural production have been identified. This organization demonstrates a high level of social and economic organization. Agriculture was one of the foundations of Caral’s economy. Through irrigation systems and terraces, they managed to cultivate a variety of products such as corn, beans, pumpkins, and cotton. Additionally, evidence has been found that they also practiced fishing and hunting, allowing them to diversify their diet and obtain additional resources. Caral’s culture also stood out for its development in the artistic field. Numerous ceramic objects, textiles, and jewelry have been found, demonstrating their skill in these arts. Musical instruments such as flutes and drums have also been discovered, suggesting that music was also an important part of their culture. One of the most fascinating aspects of Caral is its communication system. A series of quipus, which are knotted ropes used by ancient Peruvians to record information, have been found. This suggests that Caral had an advanced system of writing and accounting. Despite its advanced civilization, the Caral culture mysteriously disappeared around 1800 B.C. The reasons for its disappearance are still unclear, but factors such as climate change and environmental challenges may have played a role. Location of the Sacred City of Caral It is located in the Supe Valley, about 200 kilometers north of the Lima region in the Barranca province, Peru. How to Get to the Caral Archaeological Site? To reach the Caral Archaeological Center, there are different transportation options. If you are in the city of Lima, the most common way to get there is by taking a bus from the Yerbateros Terminal. Buses depart regularly, and the journey takes approximately 3 hours. It is advisable to check the departure and arrival times, as they may vary depending on the season. Another option is to hire a tour or excursion from Lima. Many travel agencies offer packages that include transportation and a guided visit to the Caral Archaeological Center. This option can be more comfortable and convenient, as you won’t have to worry about transportation or itinerary organization. If you prefer to drive on your own, you can rent a car in Lima and follow the Panamericana Norte highway until you reach the Barranca province. The journey takes approximately 3 hours, depending on traffic and road conditions. Once you arrive in the Barranca province, you will need to take a detour to the Caral Archaeological Center. The detour is signposted, and the road is in good condition. However, it is advisable to bring a map or use a GPS to ensure you don’t get lost. It is important to note that the Caral Archaeological Center is in a remote area and does not have public transportation services. Therefore, it is recommended to plan your visit in advance and make sure you have a reliable means of transportation to return to your place of origin. What to See at the Caral Archaeological Center? The Caral Archaeological Center offers a unique experience for history and culture enthusiasts. As you explore this site, you will encounter impressive structures, including the stepped stone pyramids, temples, courtyards, and ceremonial squares. The Major Pyramid is one of the most notable structures and provides a spectacular panoramic view of the area. Here are the highlights you can enjoy: Stepped Pyramids: One of the most outstanding aspects of Caral is the impressive stepped pyramids that rise majestically on the horizon. These monumental structures, carefully built by the Caral civilization, testify to the architectural ingenuity of antiquity. Exploring these pyramids will offer you a glimpse of the greatness and technical skill of this ancient civilization. Temples and Ceremonial Squares: In addition to the pyramids, Caral houses temples and ceremonial squares that reflect the social and religious life of the civilization. These spaces were used for ceremonial activities, rituals, and community gatherings. Walking through these sites will allow you to immerse yourself in the world of ancient Caral culture and better understand their practices and beliefs. Natural Landscape: The surrounding environment of the sacred city of Caral is equally impressive. The green and fertile valley in which this archaeological site is located offers a beautiful and serene view. In addition to ancient structures, the natural landscape will provide you with a complete experience that combines history with the natural beauty of the region. Panoramic Views: By climbing the highest structures, such as the Major Pyramid, you will have the opportunity to enjoy extraordinary panoramic views of the surroundings. These views will allow you to appreciate the extent of the valley and give you a unique perspective on the distribution and planning of Caral. Opening Hours and Entrance Fees To visit Caral, it is important to mention that the Caral Archaeological Site is a protected site, and an entrance fee is required to enter. It is also recommended to hire a local guide to make the most of the visit and learn about the history and importance of this archaeological site. Generally, the archaeological center is open from Monday to Sunday, from 9 am to 5 pm. It offers a window to the past and an opportunity to understand the greatness of ancient civilizations. Don’t miss the chance to explore this wonderful historical legacy on your next visit to Peru!
